description: One status page: name, public URL, enabled, and its components with each linked monitor's current state. Read-only.
name: get_status_page

PageAccessArg.description:
Who may open a status page; the same shape as the REST `access` field. As a
write it replaces what is stored, whole.

protected.description:
Private when true: only the addresses and domains in `rules` can open
the page, by signing in on it with a code sent to their email. False
makes it public again and keeps the list for next time.

rules.description: Who can open it, up to 500 entries. Read back, these are customer data.

kind.description:
`domain` lets in every address at `value` (`example.com`); `address`
lets in one person (`name@example.com`).

PageEmailAccessArg.description: The emailed-code way in, and the passkeys that shortcut it.

enabled.description: Defaults to true; a private page needs it.

passkeys_enabled.description: Let viewers save a passkey after an email sign-in. Defaults to true.

recheck_days.description:
Ask passkey viewers for an email code again after 30, 90 or 365 days.
Omit to never ask.

session_days.description: Keep a sign-in for 7, 30 or 90 days. Omit to keep it until sign-out.

StatusPageComponent.description: One component (a curated monitor) on a status page.

group.description: Public grouping label, if any. Untrusted data.

state.description:
Current state of the linked monitor: `up`, `down`, `degraded`, `error`,
or `no_data`.

access.description: Who may open it, or null for a page never made private.

title: Status page details
